problem: Existing cross-embodiment navigation methods (IL and DRL) rely on embodiment-specific modules such as waypoint-tracking controllers, dynamics models, or velocity-to-joint converters that must be tuned per robot. DRL locomotion methods can only track velocity commands and cannot plan velocities themselves.
motivation: A single policy that maps observations directly to low-level commands for both wheeled and quadrupedal robots would avoid per-robot tuning and the error accumulation across modules. Training many random embodiments with privileged information and then distilling the experts into one deployable policy should give zero-shot transfer to unseen commercial robots.
key_idea: Train DRL expert policies with privileged embodiment information on thousands of randomly generated wheeled and quadruped robots, then distill them with multi-expert DAgger into one transformer (Nav-ACT) that maps a unified ray-based observation to a unified 14-D low-level action.
insight: Performance scales with the number of random embodiments used in distillation (128, 1024, 4096 in Fig. 7), which suggests the policy implicitly infers embodiment parameters from proprioception history. DAgger beats offline BC (Go2 SR 69.5 vs 65.3; Jackal 88.3 vs 86.3) and L2 loss beats L1 (Go2 SR 54.2 with L1). Temporal ensembling helps wheeled robots (Jackal SR 88.3 vs 76.3 without) but hurts quadrupeds (Go2 SR 43.3 with TE vs 69.5), because joint-position actions need real-time reactivity.
method: Stage 1 expert policies: 5 PPO MLP experts (small quadruped, large quadruped, wheeled on obstacle terrain; small and large quadruped on stairs/grid/rough terrain), each trained on 4096 randomly generated embodiments with privileged inputs (embodiment parameters, height scan) in Isaac Lab.

Embodiment randomization: sample base/thigh/calf size and mass, PD gains scaled from a robot template by mass, FE and FEBK leg configurations; also domain randomization (friction, mass, pushes, noise, motor delay).
Game-inspired curriculum: 384 subfields of 10x10 m with box/pyramid/cylinder obstacles and quadruped-only terrains; promotion and demotion by goal-distance thresholds.

Unified observation/action: goal, reference speed, base size, last 5 frames of actions and proprioception, and 128 laser rays (90° FOV, 0.2-8 m) derived from depth; wheeled proprioception zero-padded; 14-D action (2 velocities + 12 joint targets).

Nav-ACT: linear observation encoder, observation sequence of 4 steps, transformer decoder (2 layers, 4 heads, 256 dim) with learnable positional queries producing a 6-step action chunk in one pass, trained with MSE.
Multi-expert DAgger: all random embodiments roll out with Nav-ACT while the matching expert labels actions, aggregating chunks.
Inference: temporal ensemble with exponential weights for wheeled robots; first action only for quadrupeds.

setting.backbone: Nav-ACT transformer (2 layers, 4 heads, 256 dim), distilled from 5 PPO MLP experts (1024-512-256)
setting.training_data: Simulation only in Isaac Sim/Lab: 4096 randomly generated embodiments per expert, 5 experts; DAgger distillation on 128/1024/4096 embodiments; no real or web data
setting.observation: Depth image converted to 128 laser rays plus proprioception (IMU/encoders), 2D goal position, reference speed, robot base size
setting.action_space: Low-level continuous: base linear/angular velocity (wheeled) or 12 joint position targets (quadruped)
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab (MP3D meshes for photorealistic test)
setting.privileged: Privileged embodiment parameters and height scans for expert training only; none at test time for the general policy

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 randomly generated unseen in-distribution environments; 1000 trials per method and robot
numbers.extra: unseen robot, simulation; also A1 SR 73.1 SPL 0.62, ANYmal B SR 60.5 SPL 0.53
unseen robot; Dingo SR 84.0 SPL 0.78; Create3 SR 91.7 SPL 0.85

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 trials per method, averaged over TurtleBot2 and Jackal, indoor and outdoor

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only, no standard VLN/ObjNav benchmark. Scalability results (X-Nav-128/1024/4096 on MP3D) are given only in Fig. 7, so no numbers are extracted.
results: X-Nav beats ViNT and NavDP on all six unseen robots in simulation, e.g. Go2 SR 69.5 vs NavDP 53.1 and ANYmal B 60.5 vs 37.2. In the real world, SR is 80 vs ViNT 70 and NavDP 65 on TurtleBot2 and Jackal.
limitations: Only wheeled and 12-DOF quadruped robots are supported; humanoids and other DOF counts are left to future work.
Point-goal navigation only, no object or language goals.
Real-world evaluation is small (20 trials per method, only wheeled robots), and the two inference strategies must be chosen by robot type.
builds_on: Legged Gym / Isaac Lab (Rudin et al.)
